chapters.title: 一、奇怪的纸条
lines: 星期六早上，小雨在小区门口发现了一张黄色的纸条。
On Saturday morning, Xiaoyu found a yellow note at the entrance to her neighborhood.
纸条上写着：请在下午三点，把一本喜欢的书带到大树下。
The note said: Please bring a book you like to the big tree at three this afternoon.
纸条没有名字，也没有说明为什么要带书。
There was no name on the note and no explanation of why people should bring a book.
小雨觉得很奇怪，决定先去问问住在楼下的小林。
Xiaoyu thought it was strange and decided to ask Xiaolin, who lived downstairs.
小林看完纸条，笑着说，这也许是一个有意思的秘密。
After reading the note, Xiaolin smiled and said it might be an interesting secret.

chapters.title: 二、门口的爷爷
lines: 他们一起走到门口，那里有一位正在看报纸的爷爷。
They walked to the gate together, where an elderly man was reading a newspaper.
爷爷说，早上有一个戴蓝色帽子的人来过，但是他没看清楚那个人的脸。
He said someone in a blue hat had come that morning, but he hadn’t seen their face clearly.
小林马上想起，住在五号楼的陈叔叔也有一顶蓝色帽子。
Xiaolin immediately remembered that Uncle Chen in Building Five also had a blue hat.
小雨却觉得，不能只因为帽子的颜色一样，就认为是同一个人。
But Xiaoyu thought they shouldn’t assume it was the same person just because the hats were the same color.
他们谢过爷爷，打算再找一点线索。
They thanked the man and planned to look for more clues.

chapters.title: 三、楼下的小猫
lines: 经过花园时，他们看见一只小猫坐在长椅旁边。
As they passed the garden, they saw a cat sitting beside a bench.
小猫脚下有一小块黄色的纸，颜色和那张纸条很像。
There was a small piece of yellow paper beneath its paws, much like the note.
小林想把纸拿起来，小猫却把它推到了椅子下面。
Xiaolin tried to pick it up, but the cat pushed it under the bench.
他们等小猫走开以后，才发现那只是一个食品袋。
Only after the cat walked away did they discover it was just a food bag.
两个人都笑了，原来不是所有奇怪的东西都跟秘密有关。
They both laughed: not every strange thing was connected to the mystery.

chapters.title: 四、陈叔叔的回答
lines: 陈叔叔正在家门口修理一把旧椅子。
Uncle Chen was repairing an old chair outside his home.
听完他们的问题，他说自己整个上午都没有离开这栋楼。
After hearing their question, he said he hadn’t left the building all morning.
不过，他昨天看见李阿姨买了很多彩色的纸。
However, he had seen Auntie Li buying lots of colored paper the day before.
小雨问他，李阿姨是不是经常给孩子们讲故事。
Xiaoyu asked whether Auntie Li often told stories to children.
陈叔叔点了点头，又提醒他们别忘了下午三点的约定。
Uncle Chen nodded and reminded them not to forget the three o’clock appointment.

chapters.title: 五、选哪一本书？
lines: 回到家以后，小雨把书架上的几本书都拿了下来。
After returning home, Xiaoyu took several books down from the shelf.
一本讲旅行，一本讲动物，还有一本是奶奶送给她的故事书。
One was about travel, one about animals, and another was a storybook her grandmother had given her.
她最喜欢奶奶送的那本，可是担心借给别人以后会弄坏。
She liked her grandmother’s book best but worried it might get damaged if she lent it out.
妈妈告诉她，可以先跟借书的人约好怎样保管。
Her mother told her she could agree with the borrower on how to take care of it first.
小雨想了想，在书里放了一张写着自己名字的小卡片。
Xiaoyu thought for a moment and put a little card with her name inside the book.

chapters.title: 六、大树下的人们
lines: 下午三点，小雨和小林一起到了大树下。
At three in the afternoon, Xiaoyu and Xiaolin arrived at the big tree together.
让他们吃惊的是，那里已经来了十几个邻居。
To their surprise, more than ten neighbors were already there.
每个人手里都有一本书，李阿姨的蓝色帽子就放在桌上。
Everyone had a book, and Auntie Li’s blue hat was lying on the table.
李阿姨说，她想在小区里办一个小小的读书会。
Auntie Li said she wanted to start a small reading group in the neighborhood.
她没有写名字，是希望大家先带着好奇心来认识彼此。
She hadn’t signed the note because she hoped curiosity would bring people together to get to know one another.

chapters.title: 七、一本书，一个朋友
lines: 大家轮流介绍自己带来的书，也说了为什么喜欢它。
Everyone took turns introducing their book and explaining why they liked it.
平时很少说话的小林，讲起动物的时候特别认真。
Xiaolin, who was usually quiet, spoke with great enthusiasm about animals.
一个比他小的男孩听得很入迷，问能不能借回家看看。
A younger boy was fascinated and asked whether he could borrow the book to read at home.
小雨也把自己的故事书借给了一位刚搬来的女孩。
Xiaoyu also lent her storybook to a girl who had just moved in.
她们约好下个星期见面，一起聊聊最喜欢的故事。
They agreed to meet the following week to talk about their favorite stories.

chapters.title: 八、真正的秘密
lines: 回家的路上，小林说，原来秘密就是一个读书会。
On the way home, Xiaolin said the mystery had turned out to be a reading group.
小雨摇摇头，说她觉得真正的秘密不只是书。
Xiaoyu shook her head and said she thought the real secret was more than books.
原来住得这么近的人，只要有一个机会，就可以变成朋友。
People living so close to one another could become friends if given a chance.
第二天，他们又写了一张纸条，这次认真地签上了名字。
The next day, they wrote another note, this time carefully signing their names.
纸条上写着：下周日一起读书，欢迎带上你的故事。
The note said: Let’s read together next Sunday. You’re welcome to bring your story.

chapters.title: 一、一个决定
lines: 小安一直想去海边的小城看看，可是朋友们总是没有时间。
Xiao An had always wanted to visit a small seaside town, but his friends never seemed to have time.
这个夏天，他决定不再等别人，第一次试着自己旅行。
This summer, he decided to stop waiting for others and try traveling alone for the first time.
妈妈有点担心，问他有没有把车票和住的地方安排好。
His mother was a little worried and asked whether he’d arranged his ticket and accommodation.
他把计划写在一张纸上，又把重要的电话号码存在手机里。
He wrote his plan on a sheet of paper and saved important phone numbers on his phone.
虽然心里还有点紧张，他还是很期待这次新的经历。
Although he was still a little nervous, he was looking forward to this new experience.

chapters.title: 二、出发前的晚上
lines: 出发前的晚上，小安把想带的东西都放在床上。
The night before leaving, Xiao An put everything he wanted to take on his bed.
衣服、水杯、雨伞和几本书，几乎把整个床都占满了。
Clothes, a water bottle, an umbrella and several books almost covered the entire bed.
他发现，如果全带上，背包可能比旅行本身还让人累。
He realized that if he took everything, the backpack might be more tiring than the trip itself.
于是他只留下真正需要的东西，把三本书换成了一本。
So he kept only what he really needed and reduced three books to one.
收拾好以后，他终于明白，准备得好不等于带得多。
After packing, he finally understood that being well prepared didn’t mean taking a lot.

chapters.title: 三、差一点走错
lines: 第二天，小安很早就到了车站，觉得自己有足够的时间。
The next day, Xiao An reached the station early and thought he had plenty of time.
可是看见人群往一个方向走，他也跟着走了过去。
But when he saw a crowd heading in one direction, he followed them.
走到入口才发现，那边的车并不是去海边的。
Only at the entrance did he realize that service wasn’t going to the coast.
他赶紧拿出车票，请工作人员帮他确认正确的地方。
He quickly took out his ticket and asked a staff member to confirm where he should go.
工作人员指了指另一边，提醒他要看车次，不能只跟着别人走。
The staff member pointed to the other side and reminded him to check the service number rather than just follow others.

chapters.title: 四、窗边的邻座
lines: 上车以后，小安找到座位，旁边坐着一位带花的阿姨。
After boarding, Xiao An found his seat beside a woman carrying flowers.
阿姨问他是不是去看朋友，他说自己只是想去看看海。
She asked whether he was visiting friends; he said he simply wanted to see the sea.
听说他第一次一个人旅行，阿姨给他介绍了一个安静的小市场。
Hearing it was his first solo trip, she told him about a quiet little market.
她说，市场没有那么有名，却能看到当地人每天怎样生活。
She said the market wasn’t particularly famous, but showed how local people lived each day.
小安把名字记下来，觉得旅途中最有用的消息不一定都在网上。
Xiao An wrote down the name, thinking the most useful travel information wasn’t always online.

chapters.title: 五、房间还没准备好
lines: 到了住的地方，小安才知道房间还没有打扫完。
When he reached his accommodation, Xiao An learned that his room hadn’t been cleaned yet.
他本来想马上休息，听到这个消息，心里有点失望。
He had hoped to rest right away and felt a little disappointed.
前台向他道歉，并提出可以先替他保管背包。
The receptionist apologized and offered to store his backpack in the meantime.
小安问清楚大概还要等多久，又确认了回来取行李的办法。
Xiao An asked roughly how long the wait would be and confirmed how to collect his bag later.
放下背包以后，他决定先去附近吃饭，不让一个小变化影响整天的心情。
After leaving his bag, he decided to eat nearby rather than let a small change spoil his whole day.

chapters.title: 六、市场里的一顿饭
lines: 小市场比小安想象的热闹，空气里都是饭菜的香味。
The little market was livelier than Xiao An had imagined, with the smell of food everywhere.
一家小店没有图片菜单，他有几个菜名看不懂。
One stall had no picture menu, and he didn’t understand several dish names.
他没有随便点，而是问老板哪一道不辣、份量又不会太大。
Rather than order at random, he asked the owner which dish wasn’t spicy and wasn’t too large.
老板耐心地解释，还告诉他一个人点两道菜可能吃不完。
The owner explained patiently and said two dishes might be too much for one person.
吃完以后，小安觉得，愿意开口问，比假装什么都懂有用多了。
After eating, Xiao An felt that being willing to ask was much more useful than pretending to understand everything.

chapters.title: 七、突然下雨了
lines: 下午，小安沿着海边慢慢走，想找一个地方看日落。
That afternoon, Xiao An walked slowly along the shore, looking for somewhere to watch the sunset.
没想到天空突然暗了下来，很快就下起了大雨。
Unexpectedly, the sky darkened and heavy rain soon began.
他虽然带了伞，鞋子还是被雨水弄湿了。
Although he had an umbrella, his shoes still got wet.
附近书店的老板看见他，招呼他进去躲一会儿雨。
The owner of a nearby bookshop saw him and invited him inside to shelter from the rain.
坐在窗边听雨的时候，小安发现，这也是计划以外的一种快乐。
Sitting by the window listening to the rain, Xiao An discovered an unexpected kind of happiness.

chapters.title: 八、书店里的聊天
lines: 书店老板问小安，为什么会一个人来这个小城。
The bookshop owner asked Xiao An why he had come to the town alone.
小安说，他想试试自己做决定，也想知道离开熟悉的环境会怎样。
Xiao An said he wanted to try making his own decisions and see what leaving familiar surroundings felt like.
老板笑着说，一个人旅行不代表一路上都必须一个人。
The owner smiled and said traveling alone didn’t mean having to be alone the whole way.
有时候，问一句问题或者分享一个故事，就能认识一个新朋友。
Sometimes asking a question or sharing a story was enough to make a new friend.
雨停以后，小安买了一张明信片，把书店的名字认真地写在背面。
After the rain stopped, Xiao An bought a postcard and carefully wrote the bookshop’s name on the back.

chapters.title: 九、给家里打电话
lines: 晚上，小安给妈妈打电话，告诉她自己已经回到房间了。
That evening, Xiao An called his mother and told her he was back in his room.
妈妈问他今天顺不顺利，他想了想，没有只回答很好。
She asked whether his day had gone smoothly. He paused and didn’t simply say it had been good.
他讲了差点走错路、等房间和突然下雨的事情，也讲了遇到的好心人。
He told her about almost going the wrong way, waiting for his room, the sudden rain, and the kind people he’d met.
妈妈听完说，她最放心的不是他没遇到问题，而是他知道怎样处理。
After listening, his mother said what reassured her most wasn’t avoiding problems, but knowing how to deal with them.
挂了电话，小安觉得自己好像真的长大了一点。
After hanging up, Xiao An felt as though he really had grown up a little.

chapters.title: 十、带回家的东西
lines: 回家的时候，小安的背包里没有很多礼物，只有一本书和一张明信片。
On his way home, Xiao An’s backpack held few gifts—just a book and a postcard.
可是他心里装着市场的声音、海的颜色，还有几段难忘的聊天。
But he carried the sounds of the market, the color of the sea, and several memorable conversations in his mind.
朋友问他，一个人旅行是不是很孤单。
A friend asked whether traveling alone had been lonely.
他说，有时候会，但也因此更愿意注意周围的人，主动开口。
He said it sometimes had been, but that made him more willing to notice people around him and start conversations.
下一次他也许会和朋友一起去，不过他已经不再害怕独自出发。
Next time he might go with friends, but he was no longer afraid of setting off alone.
